methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.

original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

actual_scope: Whether the g=13, q=8 paired-star profile exists when full projectors need not commute. This package proves the consecutive-halves subcase needs at least ceil(g/2) thin maps, so five maps are impossible in that schedule. Interleaved words stay open.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed caller or query demand removes real work, and its first experiment points at the paired-star objections in #5747 before an excluded schedule is rebuilt. The assigned question is the unconstructed g=13, q=8 profile inside that contract. The result narrows to words whose stage halves are adjacent and proves a map-count there. It does not change the caller boundary or admit a supplier.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper paired-star caller would need a complete endpoint whose thin queries actually cost less than the sharp consecutive-halves word. Five rank-q maps meet the rank floor and still fail when halves stay adjacent, so that schedule does not remove the extra maps.
stop_rule: Prove the consecutive-halves count or supply an explicit interleaved five-map word. Do not treat a failed search as nonexistence, do not lift the g=3 census, and do not change kappa.
evidence: PROOF.md together with verify.py. The g<=5 grids are complete polynomial checks. The g=13 points check the interpreter against the Laurent formula.

open_questions.question: Does an interleaved word meet the g=13, q=8 endpoint with five rank-q thin maps when full projectors need not commute?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Five rank-q maps meet the paired rank floor, and the consecutive-halves theorem does not apply once a call sits between the halves of a stage. That is the remaining algebraic form of the profile.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one explicit pattern that separates at least one stage's halves, impose the constant thin maps forced by setting every D_j = 1, and test the normalized coefficient at two field points before any native bill.
open_questions.blocked_by: No interleaved word is supplied. The consecutive-halves proof does not cover a pattern with a call between a stage's halves.

open_questions.question: Does an interleaved five-map word exist for the g=31, q=26 profile?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The adjacent-halves corollary says five maps are too few for that profile only when every stage's halves are adjacent. The interleaved question is a different profile and was not investigated.
open_questions.first_step: Keep it in its own session. Do not read a g=13 consecutive-halves proof as a decision about an interleaved 31-leaf word.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package stops at the consecutive-halves hypothesis and does not search or exclude interleaved 31-leaf words.
